script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Morning, Sarah. November 15th, 2026. Another week beginning, huh?
script.ja: おはようございます、サラさん。2026年11月15日ですね。また一週間が始まりましたね。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: Good morning, Alex. Feels like it was just Friday. You look a bit tired.
script.ja: アレックス、おはよう。まだ金曜日だった気がするわ。少し疲れてるみたいね。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Yeah, the baby decided 3 AM was party time. But hey, coffee's working its magic now. Welcome to The Daily Tanu-chan Show, everyone!
script.ja: ええ、うちの子が午前3時をパーティータイムに決めたみたいで。でも、コーヒーが効いてきました。皆さん、『今日のタヌちゃんショー』へようこそ！

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: It's overcast out there today, isn't it? I saw a few drops earlier.
script.ja: 今日は曇り空ね。さっき少し雨が降ったみたい。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Oh, really? I didn't even notice. The forecast said a 47% chance of rain. High of 18 degrees, low of 11. Not too bad for mid-November.
script.ja: あ、そうなんですか？全然気づきませんでした。天気予報では降水確率47%って言ってましたね。最高18度、最低11度。11月半ばにしては悪くないですね。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: No, it's pretty mild. I'm glad it's not freezing yet. My kids are still debating if they need coats.
script.ja: そうね、かなり穏やかだわ。まだ凍えるほどじゃなくてよかった。うちの子たちはまだコートが必要か悩んでるわ。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: I jump at everything these days. Pretty sure it's the baby. Anyway, did you see the news about the abductions?
script.ja: 最近、何でもかんでも飛び上がっちゃうんですよ。きっと子供のせいですね。そういえば、拉致問題のニュース見ました？

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: I did. Megumi Yokota's mother renewed her call for a solution. It's been 49 years.
script.ja: ええ、見ました。横田めぐみさんのお母様が、解決を改めて訴えていたわね。もう49年になるのね。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: That's just heartbreaking. I mean, to still be fighting for that after so long. It must be so difficult.
script.ja: 本当に胸が痛みますね。そんなに長い間、ずっと戦い続けるなんて。とても大変でしょうね。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: It truly is. It's one of those ongoing issues that you wish could finally be resolved.
script.ja: ええ、本当に。いつか解決してほしいと願う、終わりのない問題の一つね。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Yeah. And then, there was another story about home monitoring cameras gaining ground as a security tool here in Japan.
script.ja: そうですね。それから、日本で防犯カメラが防犯ツールとして普及しているという別のニュースもありましたね。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: Yes, I read about that. A man was caught prowling a vacant house. It's good for security, but I sometimes wonder about privacy too.
script.ja: ええ、読んだわ。空き家をうろつく男がカメラに映っていたらしいわね。防犯には良いけれど、プライバシーも気になる時があるわ。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Right? I mean, at my office, I feel like we're always trying to figure out how to make things more secure without making everyone feel like they're being watched constantly. It's a tricky balance.
script.ja: ですよね？僕の会社でも、常に監視されてる感じを与えずに、どうやってセキュリティを強化するか考えてる気がします。難しいバランスですよね。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: It is. The more technology we have, the more those issues tend to get more complicated, sometimes even exacerbated.
script.ja: そうね。技術が進むほど、そういう問題は複雑になりがちで、時には悪化することもあるわね。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Exacerbated? What does that mean?
script.ja: 「Exacerbated」？どういう意味ですか？

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: It means to make something bad even worse. Like a problem or a situation getting more severe.
script.ja: それは、何か悪いことをさらに悪くする、という意味よ。問題や状況がより深刻になる、といった感じね。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Oh, I see. Yeah, that makes sense. Like how a small scratch can get really bad if you don't take care of it. That’s a good word. Thank you.
script.ja: ああ、なるほど。ええ、納得です。小さな傷も手入れしないとひどくなる、みたいな。いい言葉ですね。ありがとうございます。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: You're welcome. And on a lighter note, did you see the story about Hiroko Machida's academy launching digital reproductions of national treasures?
script.ja: どういたしまして。それから、少し明るい話題だけど、町田ひろ子さんのアカデミーが国宝のデジタル複製を発表したというニュースは見た？

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: I did! Interior art. That sounds pretty cool. Imagine having famous ancient Japanese art on your wall, but in high quality and not costing a fortune.
script.ja: 見ましたよ！インテリアアートですか。かなりかっこいいですよね。有名な日本の古美術が壁にあって、しかも高品質で、ものすごいお金がかかるわけじゃないなんて。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: It's a nice way to bring culture into everyday life. I think it'll be popular.
script.ja: 文化を日常生活に取り入れる良い方法ね。人気が出ると思うわ。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: My office probably won't be putting up digital reproductions of ancient scrolls any time soon, though. Not really our vibe.
script.ja: 僕のオフィスは、当分、古文書のデジタル複製を飾ることはないでしょうね。うちの雰囲気とはちょっと違うんで。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: Perhaps not. Hey, speaking of Japanese culture, do you know what day it is today, November 15th?
script.ja: そうね。ところで、日本の文化といえば、今日11月15日が何の日か知ってる？

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Hmm, today? I'm not sure. Is it something specific?
script.ja: うーん、今日ですか？よく分かりません。何か特別な日ですか？

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: It's traditionally Shichi-Go-San, 七五三. The festival for children turning three, five, and seven.
script.ja: 伝統的に七五三の日よ。3歳、5歳、7歳になる子供たちのお祝いね。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Oh, right! I totally forgot about that. My little one is about a year and a half now, so we're a ways off, but I'll have to remember that.
script.ja: ああ、そうか！完全に忘れてました。うちの子は今1歳半くらいなので、まだ先ですけど、覚えておかないと。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: You've got some time. My son went when he was five. It's a nice tradition.
script.ja: まだ時間はあるわね。うちの息子は5歳の時に行ったわ。良い伝統よ。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: I can already picture it. The traditional clothes, the shrine visit... I'm looking forward to it, actually. And maybe after that, some really good ramen.
script.ja: もう想像できますね。伝統的な服を着て、神社にお参りして…。実はそれが楽しみなんですよ。その後は、すごく美味しいラーメンとか。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: You're always thinking about ramen.
script.ja: いつもラーメンのこと考えてるわね。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: I know, I know. But there's this one place, a tonkotsu ramen, it's so rich and creamy. I've been dreaming about it. Or sometimes a lighter shio ramen is perfect. It just depends on the day, right?
script.ja: 分かってます、分かってますよ。でも、あるんですよ、このお店の豚骨ラーメンが、すごく濃厚でクリーミーで。夢に出てくるくらい。それか、時にはあっさりした塩ラーメンが完璧だったり。その日の気分次第ですよね？

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: It does. Well, I think that's all for today, Alex. I've got a meeting soon.
script.ja: そうね。じゃあ、今日はこれで終わりかしら、アレックス。私、もうすぐ会議があるの。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Okay, Sarah. Thanks as always. I'll see you tomorrow.
script.ja: 分かりました、サラさん。いつもありがとうございます。また明日。
